answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded reputation with slow trust accrual: each identity must lock a refundable deposit and earn standing only through verified, useful work over weeks, not minutes. Creating thousands of fakes then costs real capital plus the time to fake a history, while a whisper of suspicion — failed checks or duplicate behavior — triggers a review that can slash the bond. Like crossing a wide mesa, an attacker pays for every step, so Sybil farms become uneconomical before they can outvote honest agents, while genuine reputation blooms like a lotus, slowly and verifiably.
